n_justification: 200 games per (m, alpha) cell in the main arm: 4 m-values x 5 levels x 200 = 4000 games, plus 800 in the D1 scale control (100/cell x 4 m x 2 levels), 400 in the D2 lambda control and 400 solver re-solves in K3 — 5600 games solved in total. The Spearman null SD at n=200 is 1/sqrt(n-1) = 0.071, so the survival ceiling 0.35 sits ~4.9 null-SD from zero, and the primary quantity gap(m) — a difference of two independent rho estimates, SD ~ 0.100 — is resolved against a reference gap of ~1.24 at better than 12 SD, so the 50% shrink threshold (a 0.62 change in gap) is ~6 SD away from the null of no change. The criterion is therefore genuinely resolvable at this n rather than a coin flip dressed as a threshold. n = 200 is chosen as 2x the F-0004 design with the first 100 games of each m=3 cell IDENTICAL to that design, so the replication anchor is exact while the primary statistics get a sqrt(2) tighter interval. The K3 arms use exactly reference_n = 100 games because their criterion is a PAIRED difference against the published reference numbers, which were computed on precisely those 100 games; adding games there would break the pairing that makes a 0.05 bar meaningful. The D1/D2 controls use 100/cell (null SD 0.100): they are diagnostics reported with CIs, and D1's binding use is a VERDICT comparison, which is robust to the wider interval in a way a point-estimate comparison would not be. Compute is the binding constraint on going further: measured steady-state cost is 0.044 s/game at m=3 rising to 0.275 s/game at m=6, so the full design is ~15 minutes; doubling n again would buy a sqrt(2) on intervals that are already an order of magnitude inside the registered thresholds. CORRECTION, post-run (red-team objection O-3): the registered text above says '5600 games solved in total'. That number is wrong in both directions and n is NOT 5600. Distinct games drawn: 4000 (main, 4 m x 5 levels x 200) + 800 (D1) + 400 (D2) = 5200, and that is the n recorded in this artifact. Total solves: those 5200 once each, plus 800 in K3 — 2 arms x 2 levels x 100 games x 2 solves per game, because each K3 game is solved by BOTH the reference damped solver and the arm solver so the comparison is paired — = 6000 solves. The 400 K3 'games' are RE-DRAWS of games already counted in the main m=3, alpha in {0.85, 0.95} cells (the same seed family, by design, since K3's 0.05 bar is only meaningful on identical games), so they contribute solves and paired comparisons but no additional sample. The registered figure added the 400 re-draws as if they were new games while omitting the 400 duplicate reference solves; the two errors do not cancel.
